questions.stem: A 64-year-old man is treated for a urinary tract infection. Nine days into therapy he develops sudden pain and swelling at the back of his heel while climbing stairs. Which antibiotic class is most likely responsible for this adverse effect?

explanation.summary: Fluoroquinolones carry a characteristic risk of tendon injury.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unnecessary antibiotic use exposes patients to class-specific toxicities. Fluoroquinolone-associated tendon injury is the classic example, alongside aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity and tetracycline photosensitivity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycosides are characteristically associated with nephrotoxicity, not tendon injury.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carbapenems are not linked to tendon injury in this lecture; they are reserved for resistant Gram-negatives.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Penicillins are best known for commonly reported allergy, not tendon disruption.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tetracyclines are associated with photosensitivity, an increased risk of sunburn.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman has had four urinary tract infections this year, each treated with ciprofloxacin. Her current urine culture grows E. coli that no longer responds to ciprofloxacin. Which statement best explains how repeated treatment led to this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin directed the bacteria to deliberately build resistance

choices.label: B
choices.text: Drug exposure killed susceptible cells, letting resistant ones expand

choices.label: C
choices.text: E. coli is inherently unaffected by this drug because of its outer membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: Her immune system lost the ability to clear Gram-negative bacteria

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug was inactivated in the urine before it reached the bacteria

explanation.summary: Antibiotic exposure exerts selection pressure that favors survival of resistant bacteria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Selection pressure means antibiotic exposure suppresses or eliminates susceptible bacteria while organisms carrying resistance traits survive and proliferate. Antibiotics select for resistance rather than causing bacteria to intentionally develop it.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibiotics select for resistant organisms; bacteria do not intentionally develop resistance in response to the drug.
whyWrongByChoice.C: That describes intrinsic resistance of E. coli to vancomycin, not to ciprofloxacin, which previously worked.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Host immunity does not explain a change in the organism's susceptibility profile.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nothing suggests drug degradation outside the bacteria; the organism itself changed in susceptibility.

questions.stem: A microbiology student notes that vancomycin has no activity against any E. coli isolate tested, including strains never previously exposed to antibiotics. What best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A plasmid-borne beta-lactamase hydrolyzes the drug

choices.label: B
choices.text: A point mutation altered the drug's binding site in each strain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Efflux pumps acquired by horizontal gene transfer expel the drug

choices.label: D
choices.text: Selection from prior antibiotic exposure enriched resistant cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Gram-negative outer membrane keeps the drug from its target

explanation.summary: E. coli is intrinsically resistant to vancomycin because the drug cannot cross the Gram-negative outer membrane.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intrinsic resistance is an inherent characteristic of a species rather than a newly acquired trait. The lecture's example is E. coli and other Gram-negatives resisting vancomycin, which cannot effectively cross the outer membrane.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beta-lactamases hydrolyze beta-lactam rings; vancomycin is not a beta-lactam, and no acquired gene is needed here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A uniform species-wide trait in unexposed strains is intrinsic, not the result of new mutations.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Horizontal gene transfer produces acquired resistance; this resistance is inherent to the species.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These strains were never exposed to antibiotics, so selection pressure cannot explain uniform resistance.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman receiving a broad-spectrum antibiotic for pneumonia develops frequent watery stools, abdominal cramping and fever on day 6. Colonoscopy shows colitis. Overgrowth of which organism is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: Antibiotic disruption of gut flora allows C. difficile to cause diarrhea and colitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibiotics disrupt the gastrointestinal microbiota, permitting overgrowth of pathogens. Clostridioides difficile causes antibiotic-associated diarrhea and colitis ranging from mild to severe, life-threatening infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candida overgrowth after antibiotics causes thrush or vulvovaginal candidiasis, not colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Enterococcus is not the cause of antibiotic-associated colitis described here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: E. coli is not the organism the lecture links to antibiotic-associated colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Klebsiella is a cause of pneumonia and resistant infections, not the classic antibiotic-associated colitis.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with suspected bacterial pneumonia was started on two broad-spectrum agents after blood and sputum cultures were drawn. On day 3 he is afebrile and improving, and cultures grow an organism susceptible to several agents, including older drugs with limited coverage. What is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a third agent to cover any organisms the culture missed

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change to a carbapenem to ensure the broadest coverage

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continue both broad agents to finish the planned course

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stop all antibiotics because the fever has resolved

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch to a narrow-spectrum drug the isolate is susceptible to

explanation.summary: Culture and susceptibility results should prompt de-escalation to the narrowest effective agent.
explanation.whyCorrect: Empiric therapy is reassessed once the organism and its susceptibilities are known. Definitive therapy should be safe, effective, narrow in spectrum and cost effective, so de-escalation is appropriate here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adding coverage increases exposure and selection pressure without a clinical indication.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Escalating to a broader agent is the opposite of de-escalation and promotes resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Once susceptibilities are known, therapy should be narrowed when an equally effective option exists.
whyWrongByChoice.D: He has a confirmed bacterial infection that still requires definitive therapy.

questions.stem: An isolate from a child's ear infection produces an enzyme that cleaves the four-membered ring of amoxicillin, rendering it inactive. Which compound is combined with amoxicillin specifically to protect it from this enzyme?

explanation.summary: Beta-lactamase inhibitors such as clavulanate protect beta-lactams from enzymatic hydrolysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beta-lactamases hydrolyze the beta-lactam ring, an example of enzymatic drug inactivation. Some beta-lactams are combined with beta-lactamase inhibitors such as clavulanate, sulbactam or tazobactam to protect them from certain beta-lactamases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftaroline is a cephalosporin, an example of a restricted agent, not a beta-lactamase inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic and does not inhibit beta-lactamases.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Meropenem is a carbapenem antibiotic, not a protective enzyme inhibitor paired with amoxicillin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is a separate antibiotic, not an inhibitor that shields a beta-lactam from enzymes.

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient has a Gram-negative bloodstream isolate that produces enzymes inactivating many penicillins and cephalosporins. The isolate tests susceptible to only one remaining beta-lactam class. Which class is generally reserved for organisms like this?

explanation.summary: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase producers are generally treated with carbapenems.
explanation.whyCorrect: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamases, produced primarily by Gram-negative bacteria, inactivate many penicillins and cephalosporins. Carbapenems are generally reserved for treating these organisms.

whyWrongByChoice.B: These enzymes inactivate many cephalosporins as well.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The organism's enzymes inactivate many penicillins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Narrow cephalosporins are among the drugs these enzymes inactivate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibitor combinations protect against certain beta-lactamases, but these extended-spectrum enzymes are the setting where carbapenems are reserved.

questions.stem: A Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate from a urinary catheter grows despite meropenem. Testing finds no enzyme that hydrolyzes meropenem; the lab attributes its growth to reduced permeability. How should this isolate be classified?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Not resistant, since no carbapenemase was found

explanation.summary: CRE is defined by resistance to one or more carbapenems, whatever the mechanism.
explanation.whyCorrect: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales are Enterobacterales resistant to one or more carbapenems. Carbapenemase production is an important cause, but resistance can also occur through other mechanisms, such as decreased drug penetration.

whyWrongByChoice.B: ESBL producers inactivate penicillins and cephalosporins but typically remain carbapenem susceptible.
whyWrongByChoice.C: That is a true property of Gram-negatives but does not describe this isolate's clinically important carbapenem resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methicillin resistance is not the classification used for this Enterobacterales isolate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CRE is defined by carbapenem resistance, which can occur through mechanisms other than carbapenemase.

questions.stem: Before cultures result, an emergency physician wants to know what percentage of E. coli isolates collected at her hospital over the past year were susceptible to each candidate drug. Which resource provides this information?

explanation.summary: A cumulative antibiogram summarizes local susceptibility data to guide empiric therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: A cumulative antibiogram summarizes local antimicrobial susceptibility data for isolates collected over a defined period. It helps clinicians estimate which antibiotics are most likely to provide appropriate empiric coverage in that setting.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Drug-level monitoring guides dosing of agents like vancomycin, not empiric drug selection by local susceptibility.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Audit and feedback reviews prescribing; it does not summarize local susceptibility data.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A Gram stain shows morphology and staining for one specimen, not population susceptibility percentages.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Individual culture and susceptibility results are not yet available at this point.

questions.stem: A resident attempts to order ceftaroline for a patient and the pharmacy will not dispense it until an infectious disease physician approves the indication. Which stewardship intervention does this represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clinical decision support for pathogen ID

choices.label: E
choices.text: Timely transition from IV to oral therapy

explanation.summary: Restricting selected agents such as ceftaroline, often via preauthorization, is a core ASP intervention.
explanation.whyCorrect: ASP interventions include restriction of select antibiotics, with ceftaroline as the lecture's example. Some systems require preauthorization for broad-spectrum or reserve agents, limiting use to clinically appropriate situations while preserving access when needed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Decision support software speeds pathogen identification; it is not an approval requirement.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PK monitoring applies to agents such as vancomycin and aminoglycosides and adjusts dosing.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Audit and feedback reviews therapy already prescribed and gives recommendations, rather than blocking dispensing up front.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IV-to-oral conversion changes route and does not require approval to start a drug.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman with cellulitis says she is allergic to penicillin because her mother told her she had a rash as a toddler. She has never been evaluated. Which statement best guides the next step in antibiotic selection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assume anaphylaxis is likely and choose a broad reserve agent

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clarify the history, as many such labels prove inaccurate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Defer all antibiotics until skin testing can be scheduled

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disregard the report, since childhood rashes are never allergic

choices.label: E
choices.text: Permanently avoid every beta-lactam for the rest of her life

explanation.summary: Penicillin allergy is commonly reported, but many labeled patients are not truly allergic, so a careful allergy history matters.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibiotic allergies range from mild cutaneous reactions to anaphylaxis. Penicillin allergy is commonly reported, yet many such patients are not found to be truly allergic when appropriately evaluated, so a careful medication and allergy history is an important part of antibiotic selection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Jumping to reserve broad-spectrum agents adds unnecessary exposure and ignores the need to clarify the reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Her bacterial infection needs treatment; the lesson is careful history, not withholding therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Allergic reactions range from mild cutaneous to anaphylaxis; the report should be evaluated, not dismissed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Many patients with a reported penicillin allergy are not truly allergic when evaluated; reflexive avoidance limits good options.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man discharged two weeks ago after receiving IV antibiotics now presents with fever, hypotension and no clear source of infection. Which initial approach best reflects sound stewardship?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Draw cultures, start broad coverage, then reassess with results

choices.label: B
choices.text: Start a narrow agent aimed at the commonest community pathogen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start broad coverage and continue it unchanged for the full course

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start broad coverage without cultures to avoid delaying therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Withhold antibiotics until cultures identify the organism

explanation.summary: Severe illness with resistance risk factors justifies broad empiric therapy after cultures, followed by reassessment.
explanation.whyCorrect: Empiric therapy is chosen from the likely site, pathogens, severity and patient-specific risk factors such as prior antibiotic exposure. Broad coverage is appropriate when multiple pathogens must be considered, but specimens should be obtained and therapy reassessed once results return.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Recent hospital antibiotic exposure is a risk factor for resistant organisms, so narrow initial coverage is inadequate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Empiric therapy must be reassessed and narrowed or stopped when results become available.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Obtaining diagnostic specimens that will inform therapy is a stewardship goal and enables later narrowing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Severe illness requires empiric therapy before the organism and susceptibilities are known.
